title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

relationships.phenotype: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 3, LOCALIZED OR GENERALIZED INTERMEDIATE, WITH BP230 DEFICIENCY

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DST gene (113810) on chromosome 6p12, which encodes the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen-1 (BPAG1-e, also known as BP230).

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-3, localized or generalized intermediate, with BP230 deficiency (EBS3) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DST gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous nonsense mutation within the dystonin gene coding for the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of BPAG1 underlies a new subtype of autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
checks.explanation: The 'EBS3, localized or generalized intermediate' label is OMIM's name for the disorder; the causal link to a homozygous DST mutation is stated.

checks.claim: The DST gene is located on chromosome 6p12.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST)
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene named in the paper.

checks.claim: The DST gene encodes the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen-1 (BPAG1-e, also known as BP230).
checks.evidence_quote: dystonin gene (DST) that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1, BPAG1-e (also known as BP230)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: EBS3 is an autosomal recessive form of epidermolysis bullosa simplex. It is caused by loss of the epithelial isoform of dystonin (BPAG1-e/BP230), a plakin-family protein of the hemidesmosomal inner plaque that links keratin intermediate filaments to the hemidesmosome. Affected individuals have trauma-induced skin blistering, mainly on the feet and other acral sites. The blistering is relatively mild and can be localized or more generalized. Blisters form within the basal keratinocytes. Patients do not have the neurologic disease caused by loss of the neuronal dystonin isoforms.

checks.claim: EBS3 is an autosomal recessive form of epidermolysis bullosa simplex.
checks.evidence_quote: identifying BPAG1-e pathology in a new form of autosomal recessive EB simplex
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: EBS3 is caused by loss of the epithelial isoform of dystonin (BPAG1-e/BP230).
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation, p.Gln1124X, leads to the loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and a complete absence of skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e
checks.explanation: Loss of BPAG1-e underlies the disease.

checks.evidence_quote: leads to the loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques
checks.explanation: The abstract links BPAG1-e to the hemidesmosomal inner plaque but does not say it is a plakin-family protein.

checks.claim: BPAG1-e links keratin intermediate filaments to the hemidesmosome.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not describe BPAG1-e linking keratin filaments to the hemidesmosome.

checks.claim: Individuals with EBS3 have trauma-induced skin blistering, mainly on the feet and other acral sites.
checks.evidence_quote: has lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles
checks.explanation: The blistering is trauma-induced and emphasized at the ankles, but the abstract calls it generalized; it does not say 'mainly feet/acral'.

checks.claim: Skin blistering in EBS3 is relatively mild.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not describe the blistering as mild.

checks.claim: Skin blistering in EBS3 can be localized or more generalized.
checks.evidence_quote: lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions
checks.explanation: Only generalized blistering is described for this one patient; a localized form is not mentioned.

checks.claim: In EBS3, blisters form within the basal keratinocytes.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by skin fragility due to intraepidermal separation
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions intraepidermal separation, and only for EBS in general. It does not say the split occurs within the basal keratinocytes in DST-related EBS.

checks.evidence_quote: he experiences episodic numbness in his limbs, which started at the age of 37 years. These neurological symptoms may also be due to DST gene mutation
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The paper reports neurological symptoms possibly due to the DST mutation, although concomitant CADASIL complicates interpretation.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) reported a patient from a consanguineous family who had trauma-induced blistering of the skin, mainly affecting the feet. Ultrastructural examination of skin showed cleavage within the basal keratinocytes just above the hemidesmosomes. Hemidesmosomes lacked a recognizable inner plaque, and keratin filaments were poorly attached to them. Immunostaining showed no BPAG1-e in the skin.

checks.explanation: Consanguinity is not mentioned in the abstract; it may be in the full text.

checks.claim: The patient reported by Groves et al. (2010) had trauma-induced skin blistering, mainly affecting the feet.
checks.evidence_quote: lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles
checks.explanation: Trauma-induced blistering is stated, but it is described as generalized and particularly around the ankles rather than mainly the feet.

checks.explanation: The abstract does not describe the level of the ultrastructural cleavage.

checks.evidence_quote: leads to the loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques

checks.claim: Immunostaining showed no BPAG1-e in the skin of the patient reported by Groves et al. (2010).

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2012) described another patient with autosomal recessive EBS and loss of BPAG1-e expression in the skin. The patient had trauma-induced blistering, and skin biopsy showed intraepidermal splitting in the basal cell layer.

checks.claim: Liu et al. (2012) described a patient with autosomal recessive EBS and loss of BPAG1-e expression in the skin.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to loss of BPAG1-e expression.
checks.explanation: The title supports autosomal recessive EBS with loss of BPAG1-e expression. It does not give the number of patients or say the loss was seen in skin.

checks.claim: The patient described by Liu et al. (2012) had trauma-induced blistering.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied, and it does not describe what triggered the blistering.

checks.claim: Skin biopsy from the patient described by Liu et al. (2012) showed intraepidermal splitting in the basal cell layer.
checks.explanation: Only the title was supplied, and it gives no biopsy findings.

paragraphs.text: Later reports described more patients with DST-related EBS. Their blistering ranged from localized acral blistering to more widespread blistering, and none had sensory or autonomic neuropathy.

checks.claim: Later reports described additional patients with DST-related EBS.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis revealed DST mutations in five patients belonging to three families.
checks.explanation: The paper reports five new patients and brings the total of reported cases to 11.

checks.claim: Blistering in patients with DST-related EBS ranged from localized acral blistering to more widespread blistering.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The claim concerns later reports, which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: None of the reported patients with DST-related EBS had sensory or autonomic neuropathy.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The claim concerns later reports. This paper's own patient had episodic limb numbness possibly related to DST.

paragraphs.text: The finding of homozygous DST mutations in affected individuals from consanguineous families (Groves et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2012) indicated that EBS3 is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.

checks.claim: Homozygous DST mutations were found in individuals with EBS3 from consanguineous families.
checks.evidence_quote: We now report an inherited skin fragility disorder with a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST)
checks.explanation: A homozygous mutation is stated, but consanguinity is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: EBS3 is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
checks.evidence_quote: identifying BPAG1-e pathology in a new form of autosomal recessive EB simplex
checks.explanation: Stated.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) studied a patient with EBS from a consanguineous family and found a homozygous nonsense mutation in the DST gene. The mutation lay in the exons that encode the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform, BPAG1-e, and the parents were heterozygous carriers. The mutation caused complete loss of BPAG1-e protein in the skin.

checks.evidence_quote: The 38-year-old affected individual has lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions
checks.explanation: One EBS patient is described, but the abstract does not mention a consanguineous family.

checks.claim: Groves et al. (2010) found a homozygous nonsense mutation in the DST gene in a patient with EBS.
checks.evidence_quote: We now report an inherited skin fragility disorder with a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST)

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2012) identified a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the DST gene in a patient with autosomal recessive EBS. The mutation resulted in absent BPAG1-e expression in skin.

checks.claim: Liu et al. (2012) identified a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the DST gene in a patient with autosomal recessive EBS.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to loss of BPAG1-e expression.
checks.explanation: The title supports autosomal recessive EBS with loss of BPAG1-e. It does not mention a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in DST or the number of patients.

checks.claim: The DST mutation identified by Liu et al. (2012) resulted in absent BPAG1-e expression in skin.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to loss of BPAG1-e expression.
checks.explanation: The title reports loss of BPAG1-e expression. It does not say a mutation caused it or that expression was absent in skin.

paragraphs.text: BPAG1-e binds keratin intermediate filaments through its C-terminal domain and binds hemidesmosomal components, including integrin beta-4, through its N-terminal plakin domain. When BPAG1-e is lost, keratin filaments are no longer anchored to the hemidesmosome. As a result, the basal keratinocytes are fragile and split above the hemidesmosomes under mechanical stress. Mutations that affect only the epithelial isoform spare the neuronal and muscle isoforms of dystonin. This explains why patients with EBS3 have no neurologic disease.

checks.claim: BPAG1-e binds keratin intermediate filaments through its C-terminal domain.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The binding domains are not discussed in the abstract.

checks.claim: BPAG1-e binds hemidesmosomal components, including integrin beta-4, through its N-terminal plakin domain.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss the N-terminal plakin domain binding integrin beta-4. It mentions only reduced beta4 labeling.

checks.claim: Loss of BPAG1-e leaves keratin filaments unanchored to the hemidesmosome.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Keratin filament anchorage is not mentioned.

checks.claim: Loss of BPAG1-e makes basal keratinocytes fragile, so that they split above the hemidesmosomes under mechanical stress.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Neither the split level nor the mechanism is described in the abstract.

checks.claim: DST mutations affecting only the epithelial isoform spare the neuronal and muscle isoforms of dystonin.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Sparing of the neuronal and muscle isoforms is not discussed. The abstract suggests the neurological symptoms may be due to the DST mutation.

checks.claim: Sparing of the neuronal and muscle dystonin isoforms explains why patients with EBS3 have no neurologic disease.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Not addressed. The abstract instead raises a possible DST-related neurological involvement in this patient.

paragraphs.text: Guo et al. (1995) found that mice with targeted disruption of the Bpag1 gene developed skin blistering caused by fragility of the basal keratinocytes, with hemidesmosomes lacking an inner plaque. These mice also developed severe sensory neurodegeneration, because the knockout affected the neuronal isoforms as well.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The Guo et al. (1995) mouse work is not in this paper.

checks.claim: Guo et al. (1995) found that hemidesmosomes in Bpag1-knockout mice lacked an inner plaque.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Not in this paper.

checks.claim: Guo et al. (1995) found that Bpag1-knockout mice developed severe sensory neurodegeneration.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Not in this paper.

checks.claim: The sensory neurodegeneration in Bpag1-knockout mice occurred because the knockout also affected the neuronal isoforms.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Not in this paper.

paragraphs.text: Groves et al. (2010) studied a patient with autosomal recessive EBS from a consanguineous family and identified a homozygous C-to-T transition in the DST gene. The change was reported as c.3370C-T and was predicted to cause a gln1124-to-ter (Q1124X) substitution in the coiled-coil domain of BPAG1-e. The parents were heterozygous for the mutation, and BPAG1-e protein was absent from the patient's skin.
